Every existing Control Panel trigger is re-homed onto its screen, the Control Panel becomes the index (scenario jumps, clock and reset stay there), and the HL7/FHIR tooling gets interim Future-scope badges plus an S1 caveat.

phases.title: AA fee as its own monthly invoice
phases.goal: Step 1, re-greened on its own: stop netting the 5% AA fee from the ACCPAY, so the payable equals the receivable and a part payment releases exactly the amount received (US-10.2.1); reseed billing history, remove the Xero simulator's fee block and web Payments' fee columns, and re-baseline the S3 figures. Each fee invoice has its own number, billing case and simulated ACCREC against the anaesthetist's Xero contact; it is always a separate invoice paid into AA's own account, never netted against payables (Greg, 2026-10-02: trust law). The BCTI count runs through one pure, tested function (BCTIs for an anaesthetist in a month), the only place the count is made. Later phases that add invoices (22, 36, 38b, 39, 39b) feed it and must keep it the only count. Admin and web Accounts show the fee invoice paid or unpaid, and Xero pair records carry the invoice number and reference. The horizon is a setting, four months in current practice (FT-01.1): shortening it drops far-edge days and extending it fills them. The List becomes its own record with a slotId, created on assignment: by office assignment from a free Slot (which requires a surgeon and a hospital, creates an ACTIVE List, the state 15b named, and shows Phase 17's not-preferred warning) or by the recurring-booking projection; once a List is in a Slot, the List shows in place of the status. (2) Answered provisional readings (RV-26): whoever moves a List, the office or the anaesthetist, chooses whether the vacated session becomes free or unavailable, on every path including marking unavailable (OQ-84, D60): VACATED_SESSION_DEFAULT's provisional hint goes. (3) Notices active or resolved (OQ-79, D58; US-13.8.3; re-opens 32's FT-13.8, US-13.8.1, US-13.8.2, DM-41): resolvedAt and resolvedBy on a notice, a tick on the dashboard panel and page that hides it for every admin, a 'Show resolved' filter with who and when, a count of active notices, nothing expiring, the same tick affordance as 15a's to-do Clear; NOTIFICATION_POOL_RULE's 'still being confirmed' caption goes. (4) Alert the office (US-03.6.3): on mobile and web, 'Alert the office' on a List or Booking with a note posts an active notice (a new kind carrying the note and the link) that stays until ticked; 21a shows it at review; the submit rule while flagged is undecided: submit stays allowed. (5) The office's finders order available colleagues by tier, then preferred pairing, ordering only (re-opens 17's US-13.6.4 and 28's US-01.4.2; OQ-102's 19 October note); the anaesthetist apps stay availability-only (OQ-113 answered 2026-10-29, D54: tiers and pairings order the list for the admin team only).

phases.title: Out-of-hours Lists
phases.goal: Build the out-of-hours List (US-01.1.6, Confirmed: accepted by AA, reported 5 November; its design still to do; DM-66). D84's working design, labelled provisional once and kept in one module: an admin creates, on Admin Day, an out-of-hours List for an anaesthetist on any day, today included, after the PM session, with a surgeon, a hospital and its own start time (6:00pm by default, editable), for emergency or late cases in any specialty; the one-surgeon, one-hospital rule applies (FT-01.3). It is a List with its own start time held outside the AM and PM Slots (no third kind of Slot; DM-66's second option), at most one per anaesthetist per evening; a Draft List already shows that a List can sit in no Slot. It shows after the anaesthetist's AM and PM Lists on their day on mobile, web and the PWA (and in 38a's main view), and in an evening block after PM on the Admin Day grid (the ruler extended past 18:00); its Bookings are captured, completed, submitted, authorised and billed as on any List (our reading). The availability finders and the conflict rules ignore it (anaesthetists set availability for AM and PM only), and the anaesthetist does not create one; the office may reassign or remove it. Keep 'which Lists are on this anaesthetist's day, in order' in one helper with tests, since Session is read in about 36 files. The A and B split of a session (US-01.1.5, Proposed) is parked: build nothing for it.

phases.title: Stubs on a List
phases.goal: Build OQ-118's answer (4 November, D66; Donald for the build, not yet seen by Vanessa or Ben): when an incoming booking for a List cannot become a Booking, for example because it has no NHI, a stub shows in its place on that List until the office resolves it from intake (FT-02.6, now 'Stubs on a List'). A stub is not a Booking, so the 19 October rule (OQ-49, D11) still holds: no Booking or patient is saved without an NHI, and the row keeps waiting in 33's unmatched queue. Add a Stub record (DM-58) held outside the Bookings table on an identifier of its own, never the NHI (US-02.6.1): its List, a link to the waiting import row, the reason it could not be posted and what the row carried as received (patient name, procedure text, time), created when 33's matcher places a row with no NHI on a List, from any source (a hospital row, a synced row or, from 34, a rooms' PDF row), the List's other Bookings added as usual. Draw it on the List in all three apps, clearly marked as a booking with a problem the office must resolve (US-02.6.2): mobile and web List views, the Admin Day drawer, List detail and Review; never counted as a Booking (no fee, no completion, no billing, no search hit as a Booking). A List holding one never looks complete (US-02.6.1): the stub carries 15a's warning treatment (the triangle) and the List's progress shows it as outstanding ('1 waiting at intake'); because a stub is not a Booking it registers no Booking warning and adds no to-do entry (the office's chase is 33's unmatched queue and 40's waiting view), and submit and authorise neither prompt nor block (15a removed the confirm step, US-13.7.3). Resolve it from intake (US-02.6.3): adding the NHI on the waiting row creates the Booking through 33's guarded path and the Booking takes the stub's place (our reading, labelled once); rejecting the row removes the stub; both audited, in one resolve function that 40's waiting-rows view reuses. This closes US-02.1.4's new 'Stub on the List' criterion (on 33's covers) and gives 40 the stub US-11.1.4 and US-11.1.5 now name. What a stub shows and how a List holding one reads are still to be worked out with intake: our reading, its display fields and the List's marking in one place each. Seed one demo List with a stub.
phases.delivers: A Stub record on the List for an incoming booking that could not be posted (no NHI), held outside the Bookings table on its own identifier and linked to its waiting intake row, drawn clearly marked in mobile, web and Admin List views and never counted as a Booking; a List holding one never reads all-complete, with no prompt or block at submit or authorise. Adding the NHI at intake turns the row into the Booking that takes the stub's place; rejecting it removes the stub; one audited resolve path that 40 reuses

The stub's key is never the NHI. That the Booking replaces the stub, what a stub shows and how a List holding one reads are our reading (US-02.6.3, US-02.6.2, US-02.6.1): label once, one place each. No prompt at submit or authorise and no Booking warning or to-do entry for a stub: 15a's warnings are records on a Booking and its confirm step is gone (US-13.7.3); the List's own marking carries the stub. 40's waiting-rows view and 34's PDF rows reuse this resolve path, never a second one. The display component is PWA-safe in src/shared. PERSIST_VERSION bump. Demo guide: S1's waiting no-NHI row and the cheat sheet's NHI lines.
